chunks: And from him (Al-Hilli) from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Uthman ibn Isa from Al-Mu'alla ibn Shihab who said:

Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'O my father, what is the reward for one who visits you?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son, whoever visits me while alive or after death, or visits your father, or visits your brother, or visits you, it becomes a right upon me to visit him on the Day of Resurrection and to clear him of his sins.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: The meaning of the saying of the Truth-teller (peace be upon him): 'Whoever visits the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is like one who visits Allah above His Throne.' This means that for the visitor of him (peace be upon him) there is great reward, immense recompense, and honor on the Day of Resurrection, as if Allah raised him to His heaven and brought him close to His Throne which is borne by the angels, and showed him from among His special angels that which confirms his honor. And it is not according to what the common people assume from the implication of similarity (literalism).

key_terms.حَقّاً عَلَيَّ: A right upon me (obligatory divine action)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the profound spiritual merit of Ziyarah (visitation) to the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt, promising divine visitation and sin purification on the Day of Judgment. Shaykh al-Tusi elucidates that the phrase 'visiting Allah' is a metaphor for the highest degree of honor and proximity to the Divine Throne, explicitly rejecting the common misconception of literal physical similarity (Tashbih) in favor of a spiritual elevation that confirms the visitor's special status among the angels.
